status: INCOMPLETE. Proposition summaries come from the Secretary of State's ballot language, Legislative Council analyses and publicity pamphlet, read through a summary tool; the official ballot wording itself is copied word for word from the Secretary of State's ballot language. Candidate lists are the Secretary of State's 2026 General Election candidate list, as printed (write-in candidates are not shown). Your sample ballot is the final word.
statewideNote: Every Arizona voter decides these 8 Ballot Propositions.

statewide.title: Ban taxes on miles driven, and tracking or limiting miles without consent
statewide.what: PROHIBITS TAXES OR FEES BASED ON VEHICLE MILES TRAVELED AND LAWS MONITORING OR LIMITING VEHICLE MILES TRAVELED WITHOUT CONSENT.
statewide.yes: The state, counties, cities and towns could not tax you or charge a fee based on how many miles you drive, and could not track or limit your miles unless you agree.
statewide.no: Nothing changes: the constitution stays as it is now.
statewide.needs: a majority for the three constitutional amendments (Article 21, Section 1); not confirmed for the five laws

statewide.title: Add details to the ban on race-based preferential treatment and discrimination
statewide.what: ADDS FURTHER DETAILS TO THE CONSTITUTIONAL PROHIBITION AGAINST PREFERENTIAL TREATMENT OR DISCRIMINATION BY THE STATE BASED ON RACE, ETHNICITY, OR OTHER CLASSES.
statewide.yes: The constitution's existing ban would add details: no requiring people to back race-based preferences or "diversity, equity and inclusion" ideas to get schooling, a job or a contract, no public money for positions that promote them, and no different discipline by race.
statewide.no: Nothing changes: the current ban in the constitution stays as it is.
statewide.needs: a majority for the three constitutional amendments (Article 21, Section 1); not confirmed for the five laws

statewide.title: Government-issued proof of identity for every voter, including by mail, and other election rules
statewide.what: REQUIRES ALL VOTERS, INCLUDING VOTERS WHO VOTE BY MAIL, TO SHOW GOVERNMENT-ISSUED ID TO VOTE IN EACH ELECTION; MAKES OTHER CHANGES TO ELECTION ADMINISTRATION AND CAMPAIGN FINANCE PROHIBITIONS.
statewide.yes: Every voter, including mail voters, would have to show government-issued proof of identity in each election; only government-issued ID would count. Other election rules would also change.
statewide.no: Nothing changes: the current election rules in the constitution stay.
statewide.needs: a majority for the three constitutional amendments (Article 21, Section 1); not confirmed for the five laws

statewide.title: Limit local taxes on groceries: voter approval and a 2% cap
statewide.what: RETROACTIVELY PROHIBITS LOCAL GOVERNMENTS FROM ADOPTING OR INCREASING A TAX ON GROCERIES WITHOUT VOTER APPROVAL AND SETS A MAXIMUM RATE OF 2%.
statewide.yes: Local governments could not adopt or raise a tax on groceries from July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2027; after that, only with voter approval and no higher than 2%.
statewide.no: Nothing changes: current laws on local taxes stay.
statewide.needs: a majority for the three constitutional amendments (Article 21, Section 1); not confirmed for the five laws

statewide.title: Declare drug cartels terrorist organizations and direct Arizona Homeland Security to act
statewide.what: DECLARES THAT DRUG CARTELS ARE TERRORIST ORGANIZATIONS; DIRECTS THE ARIZONA DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY TO DO EVERYTHING IN ITS AUTHORITY TO ADDRESS DRUG CARTELS.
statewide.yes: State law would declare drug cartels terrorist organizations and direct the Arizona Department of Homeland Security to do everything in its authority about the threat.
statewide.no: Nothing changes: current laws on terrorism and the Department of Homeland Security stay.
statewide.needs: a majority for the three constitutional amendments (Article 21, Section 1); not confirmed for the five laws

statewide.title: Athletic teams by sex at birth, and private spaces tied to athletics
statewide.what: REQUIRES ALL SCHOOLS AND ATHLETIC ASSOCIATIONS TO DESIGNATE ATHLETIC TEAMS AS MALE, FEMALE, OR COED BASED ON THE BIOLOGICAL SEX OF THE ATHLETES AS DEFINED AT BIRTH; PROHIBITS THESE ENTITIES FROM AUTHORIZING USE OF PRIVATE SPACES NOT DESIGNATED FOR A PERSON’S SEX.
statewide.yes: All public and private schools and athletic associations must label teams male, female or coed by biological sex at birth and keep males off female teams, bar use of private spaces such as locker rooms meant for the other sex, and athletes could sue those that knowingly break the rule.
statewide.no: Nothing changes: current laws on student athletics stay.
statewide.needs: a majority for the three constitutional amendments (Article 21, Section 1); not confirmed for the five laws

statewide.title: Ban traffic photo enforcement unless under contract by Dec. 31, 2026, with votes to continue
statewide.what: PROHIBITS STATE AGENCIES AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS FROM USING PHOTO ENFORCEMENT SYSTEMS FOR TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT UNLESS PROVIDED BY CONTRACT AS OF DECEMBER 31, 2026; REQUIRES LOCAL GOVERNMENTS TO OBTAIN VOTER APPROVAL TO CONTINUE THEIR USE.
statewide.yes: State agencies and local governments could not use photo enforcement for traffic unless they have a contract by December 31, 2026, and local governments would need voter approval at the next general election and every 10 years after.
statewide.no: Nothing changes: current laws on photo enforcement stay.
statewide.needs: a majority for the three constitutional amendments (Article 21, Section 1); not confirmed for the five laws

statewide.title: Large school districts must spend at least 60% of operating money on direct instruction
statewide.what: REQUIRES CERTAIN SCHOOL DISTRICTS TO SPEND AT LEAST SIXTY PERCENT OF THEIR OPERATIONAL SPENDING ON DIRECT INSTRUCTIONAL EXPENSES AS DEFINED BY THE AUDITOR GENERAL; REDUCES CERTAIN STATE FUNDING FOR NON-COMPLIANT DISTRICTS.
statewide.yes: Large school districts must spend at least 60% of their operating money on direct instruction as the Auditor General defines it, or lose 25% of their Classroom Site Fund money for each year they miss it.
statewide.no: Nothing changes: current laws on school district budgets stay.
statewide.needs: a majority for the three constitutional amendments (Article 21, Section 1); not confirmed for the five laws
